rows.text: Reserve {1}{R}{G} before you attack. Balthier and Fran's extra-combat payment happens when their attack trigger resolves, before combat damage. They do not untap anything or give you a main phase between combats. Your Vehicles normally stay ready for the next attack because the commander gives them vigilance.

This Bracket 3 list emphasizes early development, haste, a small number of threatening attackers, and short combat turns. Its fourteen Vehicles supply pressure and resources. The tuned version trades some expensive value and cheat effects for one-mana ramp, attack-triggered mana, double strike, and combat boosts. Ancient Tomb, Jeska's Will, and The One Ring are the three Game Changers. There is no planned infinite combo, mass land denial, or extra-turn chain. The usual plan is one additional combat, with more available when an established board makes them decisive.

guide.title: The turn you want to repeat

rows.name: Balthier and Fran
rows.text: Their four power can crew every Vehicle in this list alone. The Vehicle must actually have been crewed by them that turn and must attack in the first combat phase to trigger the payment. Other pilots crewing a Vehicle do not qualify it. Once crewed, a Vehicle stays a creature until end of turn, covering all your combats. The commander can crew immediately after entering because crew is an ability of the Vehicle, not the commander's own tap ability.

Declare your intended attacks, pay for the additional combat if it advances the game, resolve the attack and damage effects, then attack again with the available creatures. A Vehicle already animated by another effect may still be crewed by the commander to meet the extra-combat condition. Returning the commander after it was removed creates a new object; crew with the new commander if you want its ability to recognize that crew action.

rows.name: Rocketeer Boostbuggy
rows.text: A cheap Vehicle that makes a Treasure on every attack. Put the commander's extra-combat trigger on the stack first and Boostbuggy's Treasure trigger above it, so the Treasure exists when the payment is due. One Treasure pays only one of the three required mana. Its exhaust ability can permanently animate it, but the commander still needs to crew it that turn for the additional-combat trigger.

rows.name: Smuggler's Copter
rows.text: A two-mana flying attacker that loots on each attack or block. Two attacks offer two opportunities to replace unwanted cards. Discard expensive artifacts when Goblin Welder can recover them, or spare lands when your mana is already developed.

rows.name: Mighty Servant of Leuk-o
rows.text: Crew it for the first time that turn with exactly two creatures to earn its combat-damage draw ability. Use Balthier and Fran plus a spare mana creature: exceeding the minimum crew power is legal. It can then draw two cards on each successful combat-damage event that turn. Crewing with only the commander first and adding another crew activation later does not earn the ability.

rows.name: Gastal Thrillroller
rows.text: Arrives animated with haste, making it a straightforward early attacker. Crew it with Balthier and Fran anyway when you want the extra-combat trigger. Its graveyard activation provides recovery at the cost of mana and a discarded card; the finality counter means it is exiled if it would subsequently die.

rows.name: Thunderous Velocipede
rows.text: A large, trampling three-mana Vehicle that improves later creatures and Vehicles with counters. The bonus is one counter for mana value four or less and three counters above that threshold. It does not put counters on creatures that merely become animated later or on itself from its own ability.

guide.title: Make two attacks produce more than damage

rows.name: The Regalia
rows.text: Haste and crew one make it useful with or without the commander. Every attack finds the next land and puts it onto the battlefield tapped, so two attacks build future mana quickly. That tapped land normally cannot fund the current additional-combat payment.

rows.name: Lumbering Worldwagon
rows.text: Three mana buys a Vehicle and a guaranteed basic land entering tapped, with another basic available on each attack. This ramps earlier and more reliably than milling for lands, and the Vehicle's power scales with your land count. There are only six basics in the deck, shared with Prismatic Vista and any fetches that find them, so count remaining targets. The tapped lands cannot pay the current attack-trigger cost. Resolve the searches efficiently; this is a power upgrade that does add shuffling to combat turns.

rows.name: Hoard Hauler
rows.text: Trample helps it connect, then the damaged player's artifact count determines your Treasures. Those Treasures arrive after the commander's attack-trigger payment, so they cannot retroactively pay for that extra combat. Use them for later instant-speed plays, your postcombat main phase, or subsequent turns.

rows.name: Esika's Chariot
rows.text: Provides its own two Cats for crew and makes another token when it attacks. Copy a Cat for pressure or a Treasure for mana when that is more useful. The token is not created attacking and has no granted haste. The Cats lack the commander's Vehicle vigilance, so attacking with them normally taps them for the later combat too.

rows.name: Skysovereign, Consul Flagship
rows.text: Deals three to an opposing creature or planeswalker on entry and on each attack. Across two combats it can remove several small blockers or utility creatures while applying flying damage. Its triggered damage cannot target players.

rows.name: Rover Blades
rows.text: A three-mana Vehicle with built-in double strike replaces a much more expensive threat. Under the commander it is a 3/3, dealing six on an unblocked attack and twelve over two combats before any other boosts. Xenagos and Berserk scale both damage steps. Normally crew it instead of paying four to equip; becoming a creature makes it detach if it was attached.

rows.name: Professional Face-Breaker
rows.text: Turns successful attacks into Treasures and lets you sacrifice those Treasures to play cards from exile that turn. It triggers once per damaged player per combat-damage step, not once per creature. Rover Blades can therefore produce two Treasures against one player in a combat if it connects in both steps. These Treasures arrive too late for the commander's first attack-trigger payment; use them for later instant-speed plays or your postcombat development. Normal timing still applies to exiled cards.

rows.name: Reaver Titan
rows.text: Its attack trigger deals five to every opponent each combat, while its large body attacks one defender. Two attacks therefore deal ten to each opponent before any combat damage. It has protection from mana value three or less, which also prevents your own Temur Battle Rage, Berserk, Tyvar's Stand, Hunter's Insight, Shadowspear, and Kessig Wolf Run from targeting or attaching to it. Crew does not target, so Balthier and Fran can crew it legally.

rows.name: Unlicensed Hearse
rows.text: Provides cheap graveyard interaction and grows as it exiles cards. If you tap it to exile cards before combat, it is not available to attack unless something untaps it. Without cards exiled, it is naturally 0/0 as a creature; the commander's bonus can keep it alive, but losing that bonus may kill it.

guide.title: Develop mana early and keep the payment available

rows.name: Birds of Paradise
rows.text: Supplies either commander color on the next turn or helps crew a Vehicle when mana is less important. It has zero power naturally, so it can be the second creature for Mighty Servant only when the other creature already supplies enough crew power.

rows.name: Llanowar Elves
rows.text: One-mana acceleration that enables a turn-two commander after two land drops. Elvish Mystic provides redundancy. Decide whether each mana creature is producing mana or crewing this turn; a tapped creature cannot do both without being untapped.

rows.name: Delighted Halfling
rows.text: Its colored mana casts legendary spells uncounterably, including the commander, The Regalia, or The One Ring. Use its colorless mode for ordinary Vehicles. Its colored mana cannot pay the commander's extra-combat ability because that is not casting a legendary spell.

rows.name: Fanatic of Rhonas
rows.text: The commander's natural four power enables four green mana from this two-mana creature, with no spending restriction. That pays generic and green portions of your spells or combat payment, but you still need red separately. Keep Fanatic untapped until the combat payment if that is its job: green floated in the main phase normally disappears before combat. Its eternalized 4/4 token enables its own ferocious ability.

rows.name: Nature's Lore
rows.text: Finds a Forest card, including Taiga or Stomping Ground, to establish permanent colored mana. Three Visits does the same. Choosing Stomping Ground still requires paying two life if you want it untapped; Commercial District enters tapped regardless.

rows.name: Cultivator's Caravan
rows.text: Ramps early and becomes an attacker later. Tapping it for mana leaves it tapped, even if it subsequently gains vigilance; vigilance prevents tapping to attack and does not untap an already tapped creature. Do not count the same Caravan as both a mana source and an attacker for the additional combat.

rows.name: Ancient Tomb
rows.text: The acceleration Game Changer is particularly effective for colorless Vehicles and the generic portion of spells. It does not supply red or green for the commander or its trigger. Its life cost accumulates, so use Shadowspear's lifelink when the game runs longer.

rows.name: Jeska's Will
rows.text: With the commander present, supplies red mana and three cards to play that turn. Spend that mana during your main phase and preserve lands or Treasures for the combat payment. Unspent mana from Will does not normally carry out of the main phase into combat. Exiled sorceries cannot be cast between the back-to-back combat phases.

rows.name: Sol Ring
rows.text: Accelerates your artifacts and generic costs without supplying either commander color. Pair it with actual green access for early development and preserve a red source for the combat payment. It does not compensate for an opening hand whose lands cannot cast your colored spells.

rows.name: Wild Growth
rows.text: One-mana acceleration on any land lets you develop the commander sooner while preserving later mana for attacks. It adds green regardless of the enchanted land's original production. When possible, enchant a land you are unlikely to sacrifice; losing that land also loses the Aura.

rows.name: Utopia Sprawl
rows.text: The second one-mana land accelerator needs a Forest, including Taiga or Stomping Ground. Choose the color your opening hand needs, often red when your other sources already provide green. Fetch an actual Forest land type first; a land producing green is not automatically a Forest. Yavimaya can make other lands legal hosts, but losing Yavimaya can make those Auras fall off.

guide.title: Add haste and get value without the commander

rows.name: Samut, Hazoret's Champion
rows.text: Gives your creatures haste continuously, so a Vehicle gains the benefit as soon as it becomes a creature. At two mana, it lets newly cast Vehicles attack without a large setup investment. Samut also lets your tap-ability creatures operate immediately.

rows.name: Rising of the Day
rows.text: Continuous haste works on Vehicles that entered as noncreature artifacts and were crewed afterward. Its extra power for legendary creatures also strengthens the commander, The Regalia, and other legends. This is the same mana investment as the previous haste enchantment with an added offensive benefit.

rows.name: Bello, Bard of the Brambles
rows.text: During your turn, makes qualifying non-Equipment artifacts and non-Aura enchantments into hasty, indestructible 4/4 creatures with combat-damage draw. Your qualifying Vehicles keep their abilities and receive the commander's +1/+1, but their printed larger bodies may become smaller because their base stats are set to 4/4. This includes Reaver Titan. The animation ends outside your turn, and you must still crew an attacker with Balthier and Fran for their trigger.

rows.name: Grand Warlord Radha
rows.text: Generates one red or green mana per attacking creature, whether or not Radha herself attacks. Resolve this attack trigger before the commander's payment trigger. Three attackers can fund the full {1}{R}{G}; two attackers plus Rocketeer Boostbuggy's Treasure can do the same. Unlike most floating mana, Radha's mana lasts through the turn. Extra combats produce more mana, but later attacks do not produce new commander combat triggers. Radha lacks vigilance herself, so an ordinary first attack leaves her tapped.

rows.name: Ouroboroid
rows.text: Adds counters to every creature you control at the beginning of each of your combats, including itself. With no other boosts, its first two triggers add one and then two counters to each eligible creature; those counters remain after the turn. Crew Vehicles before the trigger resolves to include them. Xenagos or Tyvar's Stand can raise Ouroboroid's power before resolution, increasing the counters for the entire team. This develops lethal power during the combat turn instead of waiting for the second main phase.

rows.name: Goblin Engineer
rows.text: Finds an artifact for your graveyard and can exchange another artifact for a target of mana value three or less. It can retrieve an early Vehicle or mana rock, but cannot directly return Reaver Titan through its own activated ability. Goblin Welder is the unrestricted-mana-value recovery partner.

rows.name: Goblin Welder
rows.text: Exchanges a controlled artifact and an artifact card in the same player's graveyard. A Treasure or spare rock can become a lost Vehicle, provided both targets remain legal. The recovered Vehicle has no automatic haste. Do not sacrifice the targeted Treasure for mana before Welder resolves, because that would invalidate one of its targets.

guide.title: Keep the hand stocked with simple draw engines

rows.name: The One Ring
rows.text: Refills your hand and buys a turn of protection when cast. Returning it through Welder does not grant the cast-dependent protection, but returns a fresh Ring without the old burden counters. Bello can animate the Ring during your turn, so decide whether its tap is being used for cards or an attack.

rows.name: Sylvan Library
rows.text: Improves early draws and offers extra cards for life when you need development. Fetchlands can shuffle away unwanted cards after using Library, but repeated four-life payments alongside Ancient Tomb can leave you vulnerable to counterattacks.

rows.name: Toski, Bearer of Secrets
rows.text: Rewards each creature connecting in each combat, helping the deck keep deploying threats. It must attack if able and lacks vigilance naturally, so it does not automatically attack twice. A Vehicle army can supply the repeated damage triggers even while Toski stays tapped after its first attack.

rows.name: Return of the Wildspeaker
rows.text: Draws from your largest non-Human creature or pumps your non-Humans for combat. Crew first if you want a Vehicle counted. Balthier and Fran are Human and cannot set the draw amount, while your ordinary Vehicle creatures are non-Human.

rows.name: Hunter's Insight
rows.text: Cast on a creature likely to connect to turn its combat damage that turn into cards, including damage in the additional combat. It targets, so Reaver Titan's protection prevents you from targeting it with this three-mana spell. A large trampling Vehicle such as Hoard Hauler is a suitable alternative.

rows.name: Garruk's Uprising
rows.text: Gives your creatures trample and can draw on entry if the commander or another qualifying creature is present. Vehicles entering as noncreature artifacts do not trigger its later draw ability merely by being crewed afterward. Bello can make qualifying Vehicles enter as creatures during your turn, allowing that draw trigger.

rows.name: Faithless Looting
rows.text: Filters awkward opening hands and puts artifacts into the graveyard for recovery. It is not net card advantage. Reckless Impulse supplies two playable cards through the end of your next turn when you need additional resources; leave mana and a land play available when possible.

guide.title: Close with a few large attacks

rows.name: Xenagos, God of Revels
rows.text: Each of your combats doubles another targeted creature's current power for the turn and grants it haste. Its {3}{R}{G} cost is much easier to meet than a four-green-symbol finisher, but the boost affects one creature rather than the entire team. Crew the intended Vehicle BEFORE entering combat so it is a legal target when the trigger is put on the stack. Repeated boosts compound through extra combats. Xenagos has mana value five and can legally target Reaver Titan.

rows.name: Overwhelming Stampede
rows.text: Crew the team in your main phase before casting it, then give those creatures a large boost and trample for the whole turn. Creatures that become animated only after it resolves miss the effect. Its boost continues through the additional combat, so one spell can support two attacks.

rows.name: Temur Battle Rage
rows.text: Gives one attacker double strike and, with sufficient power on your board, trample for the entire turn. This applies in both combats and is useful on a large Vehicle without protection from the spell. It does not target Reaver Titan legally while that protection is active.

rows.name: Shadowspear
rows.text: Adds trample and lifelink to a crewed Vehicle, helping damage get through while recovering life. Equip during your main phase after crewing. When the Vehicle stops being a creature, the Equipment becomes unattached; it must be equipped again later. Its activated ability removes opposing hexproof and indestructible so your removal can work.

rows.name: Sting, the Glinting Dagger
rows.text: Equip the commander, crew one Vehicle in your main phase, then let Sting untap the commander at the beginning of combat and crew a second Vehicle before declaring attackers. If both attack in that first combat, each produces a separate payment opportunity. Six mana buys two additional combats. The ability cannot generate fresh commander combat triggers in later combat phases, so this line is finite.

rows.name: Combat Celebrant
rows.text: Exert it as it attacks to untap all your other creatures and create an additional combat. This readies pilots and other tapped attackers, but does not untap Celebrant itself. It can be exerted only once that turn; untapping it by another method does not reset that restriction. Exert also skips its untap in your next untap step.

A finishing example: with the commander and no other boosts, Rover Blades is 3/3. Target it with Xenagos before the first attack to make it 6/6, then cast Berserk before combat damage to make it 12/6 with trample. Double strike deals up to 24 combat damage. In the additional combat, Xenagos targets it again to make it 24/18, allowing up to 48 more combat damage. These are maximum combat-damage totals before blockers and prevention, require paying for the extra combat, and are not a guaranteed table kill. Without Berserk, the same two attacks deal up to 12 and 24 damage.

For a wider board, target Ouroboroid with Xenagos instead. Put the Ouroboroid trigger on the stack first and Xenagos's above it so the power boost resolves before the counter count is determined. The larger counter grant improves every crewed Vehicle, persists into later turns, and becomes larger again in the extra combat. For Reaver Titan, use Xenagos directly and Garruk's Uprising for trample; the cheap targeted tricks cannot affect its protected body.

guide.title: Protect the attack and clear the obstacle

rows.name: Heroic Intervention
rows.text: Protects your permanents from destruction and targeted opposing effects. It does not stop mass exile or toughness reduction. With Vehicles already crewed, it can preserve them through your own Blasphemous Act.

rows.name: Defend the Rider
rows.text: One-mana protection for a key permanent, including an uncrewed Vehicle. The Pilot mode is useful when a blocker or extra crew body matters more than protection, but one Pilot cannot independently reproduce Balthier and Fran's extra-combat ability.

rows.name: Tyvar's Stand
rows.text: At X=0, one green gives a creature hexproof and indestructible. Additional mana becomes a power boost that double strike or Xenagos can multiply. Increasing Ouroboroid's power before its combat trigger resolves scales the whole team's counters. Unlike some protection in the list, this targets only a creature: crew a Vehicle before casting it, and do not use it on Reaver Titan while its protection is active.

rows.name: Deflecting Swat
rows.text: Protects against targeted spells or abilities and can be free with the commander present. It does not stop untargeted sweepers or a spell whose targets cannot be changed usefully.

rows.name: Bolt Bend
rows.text: Usually costs one red while the commander is present because its power is four. It handles a spell or ability with exactly one target; it is not a universal counterspell. Losing your last four-power creature before casting means paying the full cost.

rows.name: Berserk
rows.text: One green mana doubles a creature's current power and grants trample for the turn. Cast it before the first combat-damage step, ideally after Xenagos's first boost, to support both attacks. The creature is destroyed at the next end step if it attacked that turn; indestructible from Tyvar's Stand, Heroic Intervention, or an applicable Bello effect can prevent that destruction. Reaver Titan's protection prevents targeting it with Berserk.

rows.name: Beast Within
rows.text: Answers any permanent through destruction, while Chaos Warp can handle an indestructible permanent by shuffling it away. Nature's Claim and Abrade provide cheaper artifact or enchantment interaction where applicable. Save broad answers for effects the narrower spells cannot solve.

rows.name: Vandalblast
rows.text: Removes a key artifact for one mana or clears opposing artifacts with overload. Your Vehicles survive the overloaded mode. It cannot destroy indestructible artifacts unless you first remove that protection, for example through Shadowspear's activated ability.

rows.name: Blasphemous Act
rows.text: The emergency creature wipe. Cast it before crewing to preserve normal noncreature Vehicles, but remember that Bello makes qualifying artifacts creatures during your turn. Bello's indestructibility protects those objects from damage destruction while its effect applies; if Bello dies, check the remaining board and continuous effects carefully.

guide.title: Recover and keep the sequencing short

rows.name: Eternal Witness
rows.text: Retrieves the protection spell, finisher, land, or threat the board currently needs. Bala Ged Recovery offers the same broad recovery as a spell or a tapped land early. Pinnacle Monk is another land option whose creature face recovers an instant or sorcery.

rows.name: Prismatic Vista
rows.text: Finds an untapped basic Forest or Mountain, fixing early green ramp, the commander, and the extra-combat payment without spending restrictions. A Forest also supports Utopia Sprawl. The list keeps four Forests and two Mountains as targets; Vista cannot fetch a nonbasic dual.

rows.name: Kessig Wolf Run
rows.text: Converts spare mana into power and trample on a creature, including a crewed Vehicle. A land has mana value zero, so Reaver Titan's protection also prevents this ability from targeting it. Boseiju, Who Endures adds interaction from the mana base, and Buried Ruin can recover an artifact for a later turn.

guide.title: What to keep and how to sequence

rows.text: Keep three functional lands, a cheap accelerator, and an affordable Vehicle or card-selection spell. Two-land hands need dependable early acceleration and a way to find more lands. The deck has 36 lands plus three land-option cards: Bala Ged Recovery, Pinnacle Monk, and Shatterskull Smashing. Prioritize an untapped green source for the one-mana mana creatures, and enough red and green to pay the commander and its combat trigger.

An example keep is Forest, Stomping Ground, Command Tower, Llanowar Elves, Rocketeer Boostbuggy, Smuggler's Copter, and Defend the Rider. Turn one deploy Elves. Turn two can develop a Vehicle or cast the commander; choose according to whether you can protect the setup and attack usefully next turn. Spend the following turns establishing the remaining pieces while reserving protection or the combat payment, rather than emptying your hand indiscriminately.

For a quick default turn: identify the Vehicle Balthier and Fran will crew, reserve {1}{R}{G}, crew other attackers, then attack. Resolve resource triggers that can pay for the commander first. Handle the second combat before moving to your second main phase. You do not need the multi-Vehicle Sting line every turn; use it when the additional combat is likely to close the game.

At the beginning of combat, remember three checks: which Vehicles are creatures, which have been under your control since the turn began or have haste, and which were crewed by the commander. Vigilance does not fix a Vehicle you already tapped for mana. Animation does not supply haste, and haste does not satisfy the commander's crew requirement.

The deck can keep attacking without Balthier and Fran through Bello, haste sources, ordinary pilots, and the Vehicles' printed abilities. It loses the commander's easy second combat and vigilance, so stop assuming tapped attackers can swing again. Rebuild the commander when the second attack is worth the mana, or finish through an already established boost and evasive threats.
